title: Predictable Reserve and Burst Operations PRD (draft)
body:
Summary:
A lightweight PRD proposing a predictable reserved capacity model with a clarifying burst credit system and configurable isolation controls. Goal is to give customers a deterministic SLA for baseline throughput while allowing controlled short-lived bursts that avoid noisy-neighbor failures and unexpected cost surprises.

Problem statement:
- Customers buying Dedicated capacity currently request fixed GPU pools but struggle with short traffic spikes (batch jobs, end-of-quarter traffic) that either exceed provisioned capacity or force overly large reservations (wasted spend).
- Existing autoscale suggestions are either too slow for spiky workloads or too permissive (cross-tenant bursting causes latency interference).
- Enterprise buyers demand clear isolation semantics (what fails, what gets preempted) and predictable unit costs for bursts.

Objectives (what success looks like):
- Provide a Reserve+Burst product that:
  - Guarantees baseline capacity (SLA) for committed units.
  - Provides short-duration burst capacity governed by credit budgets and policies.
  - Exposes clear isolation modes (hard, soft, dedicated) with documented behavior under contention.
- Acceptance metrics:
  - 95th percentile tail latency for baseline requests <= current SLA, even during bursts.
  - Customers can sustain 3x baseline QPS for up to 5 minutes using burst credits 90% of the time without impact to other tenants.
  - Bursts billed predictably: burst unit price <= 1.5x baseline unit cost; billing transparency in console traces.

Non-goals:
- This PRD does not propose wholesale changes to the serving runtime (no kernel rewrites).
- Not covering persistent cross-region failover or data residency features (handled in Private product PRDs).

Key concepts / terminology (explicit definitions):
- Baseline reservation: committed GPU/slot allocation with SLA/RU (reservation units).
- Burst credits: time-limited budgeted capacity units that let a tenant temporarily consume additional resources above baseline.
- Soft isolation: best-effort protection; tenant burst usage may be slowed when cluster is under heavy contention.
- Hard isolation: strict enforcement—no external tenant can reclaim baseline capacity; burst evictions are sequenced conservatively.
- Preemption policy: rules to choose which burst workloads are scaled down first (age, cost profile, explicit low-priority flag).

User personas:
- Platform engineer at a scale-up (wants predictable baseline and occasional spikes for batch exports).
- Growth PM running promos that cause short reads bursts (needs cheap, fast bursts without buying more long-term capacity).
- Enterprise security/compliance lead (needs isolation modes and auditable behavior).

Core requirements (MUST):
1) Reservation primitives:
   - API + Console: create/update/delete reservation with fields: units, region, baseline_SLO_target, isolation_mode (hard/soft/dedicated), billing_profile.
   - Reservation lifecycle events logged to audit (create, scale, expire, cancel).
2) Burst credit system:
   - Each reservation gets a configurable monthly credit budget and refill rate (tokens/min).
   - Credits consumed proportionally to excess tokens used and duration; meter includes effective tokens per tokenized request.
   - Admins can purchase supplemental credit packs or enable on-demand burst (with higher unit price).
3) Isolation behavior:
   - Hard: baseline RU can never be preempted by other customers; bursts may be curtailed when cluster saturation begins to impact hard-isolated baselines.
body_continued:
4) Preemption rules and eviction ordering:
   - Define deterministic eviction ordering: expired-burst -> on-demand-burst -> low-priority-canary -> spot-like tasks.
   - Provide graceful shutdown hooks (30s) and an API signal for clients to drain and retry.
5) Telemetry and visibility:
   - Console dashboards per reservation: baseline utilization, burst consumption, credit balance, cost-to-date, top latency tail events.
   - Tracing tags for requests that consumed burst credits. Billing logs exportable to CSV/BigQuery.
6) API compatibility:
   - Backwards compatible: default reservation created when customer first purchases dedicated capacity with default soft isolation and no burst credits unless opted-in.

Secondary requirements (SHOULD):
- Autoscaling integration for dedicated pools: optional reactive scale-out to add nodes when cluster-level available capacity > threshold and cloud quota allows.
- Canary policy for new allocation behaviors: allow customers to opt an experiment into a % of traffic using burst paths.
- Pricing experiments: tiered burst pricing for different time-of-day or capacity classes.

Operational considerations:
- Admission controller changes: admission must evaluate cluster headroom and credit balances for each incoming request.
- Cost accounting pipeline: increment burst consumption metrics at gateway and reconcile with hourly billing process.
- Capacity planner: visible forecast of shared headroom to avoid offering bursts when insufficient global spare capacity exists.

Rollout plan (phases):
- Alpha (internal + 3 customers): basic reserve + simple burst credits, console beta, manual ops runbook. (6 weeks)
- Beta (10–20 customers): add preemption rules, telemetry, billing exports, public docs. (8–10 weeks)
- General availability: hardened autoscale integrations, pricing, SLA language update, legal review. (12 weeks after Beta)

Open questions / tradeoffs:
- Credit model: time-based refill vs. usage-based top-up — which is easier to reason about for customers?
- Pricing cap: how to cap burst spend to avoid accidental large bills for small customers?
- How aggressively should hard isolation be enforced in multi-tenant clusters with fluctuating utilization?

Risks & mitigations:
- Risk: Bursts may let noisy tenants degrade cluster QoS. Mitigation: instrument per-tenant throttles and circuit-breakers; hard isolation option for paying customers.
- Risk: Complexity in billing reconciliation. Mitigation: end-to-end billing tests in staging and daily reconciliation jobs before GA.

Acceptance criteria (concrete):
- Feature parity demo: console can create reservation and purchase credits end-to-end without backend errors.
- Load test: simulated cluster with 50 tenants demonstrates baseline SLAs preserved during 90th percentile of burst events.
- Billing validation: sample invoices show correct burst line items and exported CSV matches internal meter for 99.9% of events.

Notes / low-fi mockups and UX asks:
- Console: compact card showing credit balance with hover tooltip explaining consumption rate and cost.
- API: checkout flow via REST with invoice preview endpoint.

Next steps / immediate action items:
- Product: finalize credit pricing band proposal and sample invoices. Owner: Aisha (2 weeks).
- Engineering: spike admission controller change; estimate engineering effort for token meter. Owner: Marcus (1 sprint).
- SRE/Ops: draft runbook for burst-induced preemption incidents. Owner: Owen (2 weeks).

Appendix: short example scenarios (for sales and docs)
- Burst for a payroll job: baseline reservation covers steady API traffic; monthly payroll batch consumes 10k burst credits, consumes 4x baseline for 12 minutes, no SLA impact to other tenants.
- Promotion spike: growth team buys a small on-demand credit pack for a weekend promotion; hits 95th percentile surge but capped by credit budget and hit with higher per-unit charge, predictable invoice.

Document history:
- 2025-11-12 created by Aisha Patel
- 2026-01-05 notes from Marcus Chen on admission controller
- 2026-02-08 updated with billing export requirements (Owen)

(End of draft)
